question: Why do impersonated users receive 403 on the home page?
author: Aarav Mehta
resolution: Updated the ACL script to recognize 'impersonator' roles in the session context, which fixed the 403 error.

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: Hey Aarav, can you provide the exact steps to reproduce this? Are you impersonating via the admin console or the support dashboard?

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: I'm using the support dashboard. I click 'Impersonate', type in a standard user's email, and as soon as the page reloads, I get a big 403 Forbidden screen.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: I just checked the logs. It looks like the ACL script is stripping your admin roles during impersonation, but it's not assigning the target user's roles fast enough for the home page render.

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: Try clearing your cache and using the '?debug=true' flag on the URL so we can see the role array.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: Just tried that. The role array is completely empty! It says `roles: []`.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: Ah, I found the bug. The session context doesn't carry the 'impersonator' flag correctly. I've submitted a PR to update the ACL script.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: Awesome, just tested your PR on staging and it works perfectly. Thanks Raj!

question: Login loop started after enabling the new Entra ID identity provider
author: Mike Johnson
resolution: Set the authentication cookie to SameSite=None with Secure enabled to prevent the cross-site identity-provider callback from dropping the cookie.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Just to add: this only happens for users on Safari or Chrome Incognito. Normal Chrome works fine.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: Sounds like a cookie issue. Are our session cookies marked as SameSite=Strict?

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Yes, they are. But they've always been Strict. Why is it breaking now?

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: Because Entra ID does a cross-site POST back to our domain. Safari and Incognito block third-party cookies by default, so if the cookie is Strict, it gets dropped during the redirect.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: I changed it to SameSite=Lax. Let me test... Wait, now I'm getting a CSRF token mismatch error.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: For an SSO callback, Lax might still drop the cookie on POST requests. You need to set it to SameSite=None AND add the Secure flag.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Tried SameSite=None with Secure=true. That fixed it! The login loop is gone in Safari. Pushing to prod.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: Great job! I'll add a regression test for this specific flow.

question: Large PDF attachments silently fail near the end of upload
author: Raj Patel
resolution: Increased the Nginx client_max_body_size to 50M and aligned the gateway validation limits.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: Raj, how large are the PDFs? I'm able to upload a 2MB file without issues.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: They are around 15MB. The progress bar goes all the way to 100%, spins for a second, and then the file just doesn't appear in the list. No error message on the UI.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Check the Network tab. What HTTP status code is returning?

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: It's returning a 413 Payload Too Large. Ah, but the UI isn't handling that specific error code, which is why it fails silently.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: Where is the 413 coming from? The Node app or the Nginx gateway?

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Definitely Nginx. I think default `client_max_body_size` is 1MB. Let me check the config.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Yep, it's set to 10MB in the gateway. I'll bump it to 50MB.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: Thanks Mike. Can someone also add an error handler in the React UI so 413s show an actual toast notification?

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: I'll handle the UI toast. The upload limit is fixed now, tested with a 40MB file.

question: Users are receiving duplicate email notifications when a case is updated
author: Priya Shah
resolution: Implemented idempotency keys based on event IDs so the email service ignores duplicate delivery attempts.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: Every time a case is marked 'Resolved', the customer gets two identical emails separated by about 30 seconds.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: Is the webhook firing twice from the case system? Check the payload logs.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: No, the webhook log only shows one event being dispatched.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: I bet it's the Kafka consumer group. We scaled up the email workers yesterday. If a worker takes too long to generate the PDF attachment, it might not commit the offset in time, causing another worker to pick up the same message.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: That makes sense. We can increase the `max.poll.interval.ms` so it doesn't time out.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: We could, but that's a band-aid. We really need idempotency on the email sender. If we hash the event ID and store it in Redis for 24h, the second worker will just skip it.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: I'll implement the Redis idempotency key. It's safer.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: Fix is deployed. Checked the logs and we are successfully catching and ignoring the duplicate deliveries now!

question: Global search keeps loading forever when a date filter is applied
author: Daniel Kim
resolution: Added a composite index on (status, created_at) and implemented a 10-second query timeout.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: I can reproduce this. If I search without a date, it returns in 200ms. If I add 'Last 7 days', the spinner just hangs.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: Can you run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the generated SQL query?

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: Wow, it's doing a sequential scan on a 50 million row table. It's ignoring the search index entirely.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: We have an index on the date column though. Why isn't it using it?

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: Because the query filters on both `status` and `created_at`. Postgres planner thinks a seq scan is cheaper than combining two separate indices for this distribution. We need a composite index on `(status, created_at)`.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: I'll create the composite index concurrently so we don't lock the table. Give me a few minutes.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: While you do that, I'm adding a timeout to the search API. Hanging forever is terrible UX; it should at least error out after 10 seconds.

replies.author: Elena Garcia
replies.text: Index is built. The query is now using it and executing in 40ms!

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: Awesome. The API timeout is merged too. We're fully resolved.

question: Redis cache eviction policy causing high latency during peak hours
author: Sarah Connor
resolution: Switched Redis eviction policy from allkeys-lru to volatile-lru and increased maxmemory to 4GB.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: I noticed the API response times spike to 800ms around 2 PM. The Redis metrics show a massive eviction rate.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: We are currently using allkeys-lru. It might be throwing away active session tokens.

replies.author: Raj Patel
replies.text: Let's switch to volatile-lru so it only evicts keys with a TTL set. I'll also bump the memory limit up.

replies.author: Sarah Connor
replies.text: Deployed the change. Latency is back down to 40ms. Great catch.

question: API latency spikes due to aggressive Redis cache evictions
author: Mike Johnson
resolution: Configured Redis to use volatile-lru eviction and scaled the cluster size.

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: We are seeing intermittent 504 Gateway Timeouts. It looks like Redis is struggling to keep up with writes.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: The memory limit is constantly maxed out, triggering continuous evictions. What policy are we on?

replies.author: Priya Shah
replies.text: It's set to allkeys-random right now in the secondary cluster. We should match the primary and use volatile-lru.

replies.author: Mike Johnson
replies.text: Done. I also added another shard to the cluster. Error rates dropped to zero.

question: High cache miss rate and slow response times on product catalog
author: Nisha Rao
resolution: Adjusted Redis maxmemory-policy to volatile-lru to protect long-lived catalog items.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: The product catalog is taking over 2 seconds to load. Database CPU is at 90%.

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: It seems the catalog cache keys are being evicted almost immediately by Redis.

replies.author: Aarav Mehta
replies.text: Our eviction policy is dumping them because they don't have a TTL, but we need them to persist. Let's enforce volatile-lru.

replies.author: Nisha Rao
replies.text: Fix applied. The cache hit rate is back to 95% and DB CPU is stabilizing at 30%.

question: Kubernetes Pods crashing with OOMKilled out of memory errors
author: Daniel Kim
resolution: Optimized the memory buffer allocation and adjusted the garbage collection parameters for Memory leaks in the data pipeline.

replies.author: Daniel Kim
replies.text: This is a detailed technical reply regarding Memory leaks in the data pipeline. We have checked the logs and found several warning traces for step 1. The buffer allocation seems to spike momentarily during this phase, causing the orchestrator to deprioritize the job. We recommend reviewing the heap dump from timestamp 14:01:00 to cross-reference the memory leak signatures. Also, ensure that the background garbage collection is properly tuned for this environment. If we continue seeing this pattern, we might need to alter the persistent volume claim limits or refactor the batching mechanism to process 100 records at a time instead of loading the entire dataset into RAM.
